# Sirach Chapter 10 — The EMET Bible (Literal)

**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** Codex Vaticanus, Sirach 10 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-DC/SIR_010_page_001.jpg

---

**10:1** A wise judge will educate his people, and the rule of a man of understanding will be well ordered.

**10:2** As the judge of the people is, so are his officials; and as the ruler of the city is, so are all its inhabitants.

**10:3** An undisciplined king will ruin his people; but a city will be established through the understanding of its powerful men.

**10:4** The government of the earth is in the hand of the Lord, and he will raise up over it the right man at the right time.

**10:5** The success of a man is in the hand of the Lord, and it is he who confers honor upon the lawgiver.

**10:6** Do not be angry with your neighbor for any wrong, and do not act arrogantly in whatever you do.

**10:7** Arrogance is abominable before the Lord and before men, and injustice is wrong for both of them.

**10:8** Sovereignty passes from nation to nation on account of injustice and insolence and wealth.

**10:9** How can dust and ashes be proud? — even in life the bowels are decaying.

**10:10** A long illness mocks the physician; he is a king today and tomorrow he is dead.

**10:11** For when a man dies, he will inherit serpents, beasts, and worms.

**10:12** The beginning of human pride is to forsake the Lord; the heart has withdrawn from him who made it.

**10:13** For the beginning of pride is sin, and the one who holds on to it will pour out abomination; therefore the Lord will bring upon them extraordinary disasters, and he will completely overthrow them.

**10:14** The Lord has overthrown the thrones of rulers, and has seated the lowly in their place.

**10:15** The Lord has plucked up the roots of the nations, and has planted the humble in their place.

**10:16** The Lord has laid waste the lands of the nations, and has destroyed them to the foundations of the earth.

**10:17** He has removed some of them and destroyed them, and has blotted out the memory of them from the earth.

**10:18** Pride was not created for human beings, nor fierce anger for those born of women.

**10:19** What kind is worthy of honor? Human beings. What kind of human beings? Those who fear the Lord. What kind is worthy of dishonor? Human beings. What kind? Those who transgress the commandments.

**10:20** Among brothers their leader is worthy of honor, and those who fear the Lord are worthy of honor in his eyes.

**10:21** The fear of the Lord is the beginning of his acceptance, but hardness of heart and pride are the beginning of rejection.

**10:22** Rich and eminent and poor — their glory is the fear of the Lord.

**10:23** It is not right to despise a poor man who has understanding, nor is it fitting to honor a sinful man.

**10:24** The nobleman, the judge, and the ruler will be honored; but none of them is greater than the man who fears the Lord.

**10:25** Free persons will serve a wise servant, and a man of understanding will not grumble.

**10:26** Do not make a display of your wisdom when you do your work, and do not display your cleverness at an inopportune time.

**10:27** Better is a man who works and has abundance of everything than one who goes about boasting but lacks bread.

**10:28** My child, honor yourself with humility, and give yourself the esteem you deserve.

**10:29** Who will justify the man who sins against himself? And who will honor the man who dishonors his own life?

**10:30** A poor man is honored for his knowledge, and a rich man is honored for his wealth.

**10:31** One who is honored in poverty, how much more in wealth! And one who is dishonored in wealth, how much more in poverty!

---

*Translator's Note: Hebrew (Cairo Genizah MS A) is well preserved here. The central declaration of the chapter is v.12: "The beginning of human pride is to forsake the Lord." vv.14-17 are hymnic — they celebrate divine reversal. The rhetorical questions of v.19 are a distinctive wisdom device. The chapter moves from politics (vv.1-5) to pride/humility theology (vv.6-18) to the proper basis of honor (vv.19-31).*
